$description: A reproduction of the NDIS quote scenario on the live board, for local work.
Structure is copied from ISO+; all person, address and contact data is invented.
See Backend/test/fixtures/README.md before changing anything here.

bankDetails.accountsReceivableTerms: Payment due within 14 days of invoice date.

$attributesNote: The subset of board attributes that the pricing-dispatch rule keys on.
ndisPricingRules.js reads these from the LIVE ISO+ API, not from Mongo, so
this list does not drive local behaviour — it records the live state that
the item data below is built to reproduce offline. The decisive facts:
It was renamed 'OLD Direct Support Item Number' during the 2026 migration.
* 'Support Item Number' (NEW_SUPPORT_ITEM_ATTR) is present as a reference.
* A second, unrelated 'Support Item Number' of type text also exists;
only the reference one satisfies isReferenceAttribute().
Together these make boardAttributesUseLegacyNdisPricing() return false, so
the live board resolves to the NEW pricing path.

attributes.name: OLD Provider Travel - Non-Labour Cost Item Number
Provider Travel - Non-Labour Cost Item Number
Provider Travel - Labour Travel Time Costs Item Number

$itemsNote: Item.data is keyed by ATTRIBUTE NAME, matching both the webhook payload
shape and inferPricingRuleFromServicePlanData(). The three items below give
deterministic offline coverage of every branch of that function.

items.$case: Quote 17 as it stands live: opened during initial setup, almost empty. Carries NEITHER sentinel key, so inferPricingRuleFromServicePlanData() returns null and dispatch falls through to the board rule (which needs the live ISO+ API).
Resolves to 'new' with no network call: has Support Item Number and not Direct Support Item Number.

Resolves to 'legacy' with no network call: has Direct Support Item Number and not Support Item Number. Note this key no longer exists on the live board — kept so the legacy branch stays reachable in local work.

$webhookNote: Bodies as ISO+ posts them. `values` is keyed by attribute name, which is why
a rename in ISO+ silently changes backend dispatch. Replay with:
